introP1: Archives are an important part of our collective memory. They connect institutions with the past, present, and future of our communities. In the contemporary archive world, we see that not only the content of archives is important, but also how they are organized and in which infrastructures they are located. This influences the stories we derive from the archives. Colonial and oppressive structures have ensured that some stories are told while others are not, some names are mentioned while others are forgotten, and certain cultural practices remain invisible.
introP2: The Asterisk* is a tool that addresses the need to describe archival materials more thoroughly and critically. It adds new descriptions and alternative titles, expands thesauri, and approaches the material in new ways. The Asterisk* focuses on underexposed collection items and highlights previously untold stories. The more information we add to an object, the greater the chance it will be noticed by researchers and other interested parties. This way, institutions can develop towards greater accessibility and diversity in their heritage.
missionP1: It is essential to bring archival material to the present, repurpose digital infrastructures, and place archives in a broader context. This helps us move towards a post-/decolonial collection. The Asterisk* is not only a way to get involved but also a practical tool that other institutions, community archives, or researchers can use. In an inclusive digital space, creating asterisks is essential for a collection that is always relevant and in flux.
missionP2: Nieuwe Instituut works on describing collection materials and advises on guidelines for future and critical approaches to archive descriptions and metadata. At the same time, the Asterisk* will approach the collection in an artistic and experimental way to increase the accessibility of archives, for example, through featured stories on the Collection Platform. The main goal of the Asterisk* is to contribute to a better-contextualized, socially relevant, and accessible collection.
contributeP2: if you have information about an object in the collection and want to contribute to Asterisk*, or if you notice errors or outdated information.
